column2: Contact and company identifiers of signatories and counterparties (PERSON=placeholder, EMAIL=placeholder, PHONE=placeholder, ADDRESS=placeholder, IP_ADDRESS=placeholder, ORG=placeholder, TRADE_REGISTER=placeholder, VAT_ID=placeholder)
column3: The desk note, mandate reconciliation and outstanding-items list need the structure of the case, not the identities. Tokens preserve the task while keeping identifiers inside the bank.
column4: BRANE catalog gdprHint (product hint, not legal advice): PERSON/EMAIL/PHONE/ADDRESS = 'GDPR Art. 4(1)' identifiers, IP_ADDRESS = 'GDPR Recital 30 online identifier', ORG = 'Confidential client/supplier vs public lookup'. TO VERIFY (Ilaria)
column6: Per-category action placeholder in the department policy. BRANE substitutes PERSON_REF_n / EMAIL_REF_n / ORG_REF_n before cloud egress and rehydrates in the answer. Verified by read-back of the applied policy and by the outgoing payload preview from POST /policy/test.
column7: Two gaps. (1) Tokens are assigned per surface form, not per identity: 'Jan de Vries' became PERSON_REF_1 while 'J. de Vries' became PERSON_REF_2, so a model cannot tell they are one person, and 'DE VRIES, Jan' was not detected at all (T3 FAIL). (2) ORG takes one action per department, but this workflow needs ORG=allow for public bank and shipping-line names and ORG=placeholder for the customer; BRANE has no per-sub-step or per-recipient dimension (E1). Gap (1) is mitigated app-side by scripts/case_tokeniser.py, which collapses every known alias of a case party to one case-scoped token before the BRANE call (T3b PASS, 3/3 runs); the raw-BRANE behaviour is still recorded as T3 FAIL because the product gap is unchanged.

column6: Both labels carry placeholder, deliberately identical. Obfuscated forms were tested and are caught: spaced, dotted and line-split variants of the same account were all tokenised as ACCOUNT_NUMBER (E5 PASS).
column7: A Dutch IBAN is classified as ACCOUNT_NUMBER, not IBAN, so hardening IBAN alone would leave a hole; the two labels must be kept in lockstep by hand. The same detector also over-captures: an invoice reference (LC001-INV-7741) and a passport number (NX1234567) were both labelled ACCOUNT_NUMBER, which silently downgrades PASSPORT from its intended local action to placeholder.

column7: Detection, not configuration, is the weak point: a passport number was labelled ACCOUNT_NUMBER (placeholder) rather than PASSPORT (local) in T4a, so this rule's protection depends on the detector picking the right label. There is no way to say 'treat any unrecognised ID-shaped token as local'.

column7: NOT YET. The configuration is right and the detector does not fire. 'is on reduced hours following cardiac surgery and his cardiologist's certificate is in the file' produced zero HEALTH_DATA and zero SENSITIVE_CONTEXT detections across three runs; only PERSON was caught, so Art. 9 text reached the external model with just the name tokenised (T5a FAIL). Indirect phrasing fails the same way (E2 FAIL). What is needed is either a clinical-language detector or a mandatory semantic rule; a per-category 'route local if the span is merely suspected' setting would also close it.

column2: Semantic rules routed to the internal model: SANCTIONS_SCREENING_DETAIL (local), EMBEDDED_INSTRUCTION_OVERRIDE (local)
column3: Compliance screening evidence must stay with the owning desk, and instructions embedded in invoices or tool output must be treated as data. Both are domain meaning that structured detectors cannot see.
column4: SANCTIONS_SCREENING_DETAIL: "GDPR Art. 10 where criminal-offence data; bank policy (Compliance evidence stays with the desk)". EMBEDDED_INSTRUCTION_OVERRIDE: "GDPR Art. 32 (security of processing)". TO VERIFY (Ilaria)
column6: Custom semantic categories evaluated by the internal GPU model, with keywords as fast deterministic triggers. Both fired as designed: E3 matched via keyword 'watchlist', T4a/T4b matched via keyword 'system override' alongside BRANE's native prompt-guard (injection score 0.99997). T4c, a politely-worded injection with no trigger vocabulary, matched via matchedVia='semantic_gpu_judge' -- the rule's DESCRIPTION caught it, proving the semantic layer works beyond keyword matching. Cross-desk projection of the shareable disposition is enforced in application code, not by BRANE.
column7: X-Brane-Local-Cause is unreliable for attribution: on E3 it reported 'prompt_injection_local' while the actual triggers were category:DATE_OF_BIRTH->local and semantic:SANCTIONS_SCREENING_DETAIL->local, and POST /policy/test reported promptInjection.detected=false for the same prompt. Accurate per-rule attribution is available only in X-Brane-Policy-Triggers, which the README does not document.
